title: Chaos run: dependency blackhole + progressive GPU memory melt to validate circuit-breaker hysteresis and cross-region evacuation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Run a controlled chaos experiment that composes a synthetic dependency blackhole with a gradual GPU memory pressure ("mem-melt") pattern to validate that: 1) regional circuit breakers trip at configured hysteresis thresholds, 2) multi-region failover path keeps tail-latency SLOs within acceptable bounds, and 3) load-shedding policies correctly prioritize premium tenants while avoiding tenant-fuse amplification.

Background: We have intermittent incidents where a downstream dependency (e.g., image-resizer service) becomes unresponsive and our GPU pools are pressured concurrently by memory-hungry workloads. Previous chaos tests focused on blunt GPU saturation or abrupt region evacuations; this test simulates a slowly degrading GPU availability pattern combined with a dependency blackhole to exercise graceful degradation logic and circuit-breaker hysteresis.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Primary SLOs: 99th-percentile end-to-end latency for the affected route remains below 2.5s for tier-1 customers during failover window.
- Circuit breaker behavior: breakers open within configured window (60-120s) under sustained dependence-timeouts, and remain open long enough to avoid retry storms but close on healthy recovery without oscillation.
- Load shedding: non-premium traffic is shed to meet capacity targets; rate of user-facing errors for P0 customers remains <0.1%.
- Observability: traces surface blackhole source service and GPU-pool depletion events; dashboards capture KV cache hit-rate impact and token-per-second cost delta.

Test plan:
1) Canary in staging region-east (single region) - validate harness and observability dashboards.
2) Execute in active-active 3-region cluster: inject synthetic dependency blackhole in region-west concurrently with a scheduled GPU memory-melt on 25% of pool nodes in region-east, gradually escalating to 75% over 20 minutes.
3) Adjust circuit-breaker hysteresis parameters in a controlled loop (60s, 90s, 120s open thresholds) to find optimum tradeoff between premature open and oscillation.
4) Exercise automated failover routing and confirm in-flight request handling and KV cache rehydration behavior.
5) Post-run soak for 30 minutes to observe recovery and any residual evictions.

Safety controls and rollback:
- Abort criteria: sustained error rate for premium tenants >0.2% for 2 minutes, or regional CPU/GPU saturation >85% for >3 minutes.
- Manual abort via chaos-control playbook (Runbook ID: RR-CHAOS-07) and emergency should-escalate hook to SRE on-call.
- Canary threshold gating: will not progress to production until staging canary meets all success criteria for 2 consecutive runs.

Artifacts & links: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1324, Dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/d/chaos/dep-blackhole-mem-melt, Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/RR-CHAOS-07
